title: Hepatoid Adenocarcinoma of the Lung: Greifswald Diagnostic Criteria
summary:
Background
Hepatoid adenocarcinoma of the lung is a very rare type of lung cancer. These tumors show features that are usually seen in liver cancer, which makes diagnosis particularly difficult. To date, there are no widely accepted diagnostic criteria for this tumor entity, increasing the risk of misdiagnosis in routine clinical practice.

Research Question
The aim of this study is to systematically analyze the tissue characteristics and genetic features of hepatoid adenocarcinoma of the lung. Based on these findings, the study seeks to identify reliable features that allow an accurate and reproducible diagnosis of this rare tumor type.

Methods
This retrospective observational study analyzes archived tumor tissue samples that were collected during previous medical treatments. The samples are examined using microscopic and genetic methods. Only existing tissue samples and medical records are used; no additional examinations or interventions are performed on patients.

Inclusion criteria:
For the planned study, all patients diagnosed with hepatoid adenocarcinoma of the lung between 2012 and 2024 will be included. Additionally, an equal number of gender- and age-matched (± 2 years) patients with hepatocellular carcinoma, who were also diagnosed at the Institute of Pathology in Greifswald, will be incorporated into the analysis. All patients included in this study had either a moderately or poorly differentiated adeno- or hepatocellular carcinoma (tumors of grade II and III according to WHO classification).
Exclusion criteria:
No additional exclusion criteria apply for HAL patients. For the hepatocellular carcinoma control group, patients with severe concomitant malignant or chronic diseases will be excluded to ensure a more homogeneous study cohort.
